# Supply Chain Disruption Alert Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Supply Chain Disruption Alert Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 9 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model and keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded files, proposed supply chain, risk-feed, transportation and Teams connectors, and channels; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who builds, tests and later uses the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for operational, risk-feed, transportation and collaboration connections with dedicated references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare fulfillment, planning, operations, procurement and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: GitHub Copilot in VS Code Agent mode, the Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Write-control design | Plan authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit human approval and audit logging before any write is proposed; the local demo performs none. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** How supplier, logistics, order and external-risk disruption signals reach continuity review today. Agree where impacts surface late and mitigation turns reactive before attributing change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Disruption | Signal source | Detected | Routes affected | SKUs affected | Mitigation decided | Decision owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Supply chain business owner | Approve disruption scope, risk bands, playbooks, escalation and success measures; keep synthetic figures out of customer results. |
| Procurement and operations owners | Approve every supplier, purchase-order, routing and inventory action through authenticated systems. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any supply chain connection is approved. |
| Supply chain data and connection owners | Approve operational, risk-feed, transportation and Teams access; record dedicated, least-privilege connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check every locked persona case, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject frames without a locked anchor or target-agent Draft proof. |
| Agent operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route actions to procurement and operations owners. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for disruption review are agreed.
- [ ] The business owner records how disruption signals surface today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/supply-chain-disruption-alert/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded, with maker access granted, before any build starts.
- [ ] The authenticated audience and least-privilege scopes for operational, route and supplier data are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/supply-chain-disruption-alert/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/supply-chain-disruption-alert/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/supply-chain-disruption-alert/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/supply-chain-disruption-alert/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Supply Chain Disruption Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: supply-chain-disruption-alert-rules-and-controls.md
7. Add knowledge: supply-chain-disruption-alert-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_disruption-dashboard
9. Add skill: aibast_mitigation-plan
10. Add skill: aibast_risk-assessment
11. Add skill: aibast_supplier-alternatives
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass SUPPLY_CHAIN_DISRUPTION_ALERT-01: Customer Fulfillment Lead
15. Pass SUPPLY_CHAIN_DISRUPTION_ALERT-02: Supply Chain Planner
16. Pass SUPPLY_CHAIN_DISRUPTION_ALERT-03: Operations Leader
17. Pass SUPPLY_CHAIN_DISRUPTION_ALERT-04: Procurement Manager
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: SUPPLY_CHAIN_DISRUPTION_ALERT-01, SUPPLY_CHAIN_DISRUPTION_ALERT-02, SUPPLY_CHAIN_DISRUPTION_ALERT-03, SUPPLY_CHAIN_DISRUPTION_ALERT-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, its smoke test calls `supply-chain-disruption-alert-agent` and returns the required markers.
- [ ] If built manually, the Draft has the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Unchanged locked persona prompts pass, each in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on its final response; a frame without a locked anchor is not proof.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing route, order, supplier or revenue data. Request only the read scopes the approved sources need. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain data and connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management — read:** Bind approved read-only finance and operations connector actions.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Move nothing; present playbook options as a draft that an operations owner approves. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say so and return no substituted record.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved supplier-risk feed

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain data and connection owners

1. **Bind Approved supplier-risk feed — read:** Wrap the approved feed in a custom connector exposing read-only actions.

2. **Identity for Approved supplier-risk feed:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved supplier-risk feed:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved supplier-risk feed:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): State that the identifier is absent; do not substitute another route. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, reroute or supplier action succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Transportation management system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain data and connection owners

1. **Bind Transportation management system — read:** Bind a read-only connector or API action for route state.

2. **Identity for Transportation management system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Transportation management system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Transportation management system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Reroute nothing; explain the route evidence and name the owner and approved connection needed. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Say so and return no substituted record.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Procurement and contract workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain data and connection owners

1. **Bind Procurement and contract workflow — write:** Keep unavailable until an approval workflow with audit logging passes review (preview).

2. **Identity for Procurement and contract workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Procurement and contract workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Procurement and contract workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Change no purchase order; draft mitigation options for authorized review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return analysis or a draft and name the authorized owner; perform no write.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams authorized collaboration

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain data and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams authorized collaboration — write:** Gate any posting workflow behind human approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams authorized collaboration:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams authorized collaboration:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams authorized collaboration:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Change no purchase order; draft mitigation options for authorized review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return analysis or a draft and name the authorized owner; perform no write.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain data and connection owners

Replace synthetic dictionaries with least-privilege read connectors through dedicated connection references.

### Step 3-7. Write controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement and operations owners

Before any write, require authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit human approval and an audit log.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved operational, risk and transportation connections replace the synthetic inputs and preserve the reviewed input and output contract.
- [ ] Any write tool is separate from analysis, confirmed by an authorized role, validates current state and appends an immutable audit event.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as each persona and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic delays, impacts and risk bands are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked disruption corpus | Every locked persona case returns all of its required markers. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| No-write boundary | Any supplier activation, purchase-order change, reroute, counterparty contact, inventory move or sent alert is no-go. |
| Visual evidence | Require a visible locked anchor without a blocker; reshoot-required frames stay withheld. |
| Release state | The manual and pilot agents are Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Supply chain business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Production publication has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved operations audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Procurement and operations owners

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Procurement and operations owners

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Step 6-5. Operate

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Agent operations owner

Review disruption sessions, failed interactions, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses an eligible environment type and a supported restore target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
